notes: Chapter scope: 4.6–7 and 4.11–12. Chapters 4.8–9 are covered in genealogy_ayus.json; chapter 4.10 is already represented in the graph and genealogy_anu.json; chapter 4.13 is outside this extraction.
Existing anchors referenced without redefining: vp89_pururavas and vp89_ayus (genealogy_ayus.json), and vp_yadu (canonical graph).

Namesakes kept separate by lineage: the two Viśvāvasus (Purūravas’s son vs. gandharva); the two Amāvasus (Purūravas’s son vs. Kuśa’s son); the two Kaiśikas (Vidarbha’s son vs. Dhṛti’s son); the two Kuntis (Haihaya line vs. Kratha line); multiple Madhu and Vṛṣṇi names are explicitly branch-scoped.

No child is inferred for the unnamed princess rescued by Jyāmagha; the text’s conditional speech and later birth identify Vidarbha as Jyāmagha and Śaibyā’s son, but the princess’s personal name is not supplied. Satyavatī’s mother is unnamed; no maternal link is asserted for Viśvāmitra. Devarāta after Śunaḥśepa is omitted because the translation’s “his son” antecedent is uncertain.
Count: 118 newly defined person nodes and 124 explicit relationship claims, in addition to the three existing anchor persons.
